with respect to 8 of these axes we introduce 8 of the $p_{n}$ 's, and
the numerical factor
$$28(28-2) \ldots 2, \text { or } 2^{3} 8!.$$
In continuing the differentiation with respect to the next 8 axes,
the $p_{n}$ 's become converted into $\lambda_{n n}$ 's, but no numerical factor is
introduced, and in differentiating with respect to the remaining
$n-28$ axes, the $p_{m}$ 's become converted into $\lambda_{m n}$ 's, so that the
result is $2^{s} 8!\lambda_{n n}^{s} \lambda_{m n}^{s} \lambda_{m n}^{m-2 s}$.
We have therefore, by equation (31),
$$\iint Y_{m} Y_{n} d s=\frac{4 \pi}{n!(2 n+1)} a^{n-m+2} \frac{d^{n}\left(Y_{m} r^{m}\right)}{d h_{1} \ldots d h_{n}},$$
(44)
and by equation (43),
$$Y_{m} r^{m}=S\left[(-1)^{n} \frac{(2 m-28)!}{2^{m-8} m!(m-8)!} \Sigma\left(r^{28} p_{m}^{m-28} \lambda_{m m}^{s}\right)\right]$$
(45)
Hence, performing the differentiations and remembering that
$m=n$, we find
$$\iint Y_{m} Y_{n} d s=\frac{4 \pi a^{2}}{(2 n+1)(n!)^{2}} S\left[(-1)^{*} \frac{(2 n-2 s)!s!}{2^{n-2 s}(n-8)!} \Sigma\left(\lambda_{m m}^{*} \lambda_{n n}^{*} \lambda_{m n}^{n-2 s}\right)\right] .$$
$(46)$
135 a.] The expression (46) for the surface-integral of the pro-
duct of two surface-harmonics assumes a remarkable form if we
suppose all the axes of one of the harmonics, $Y_{m}$, to coincide with
each other, so that $Y_{m}$ becomes what we shall afterwards define
as the zonal harmonic of order $m$, denoted by the symbol $P_{m}$.
In this case all the cosines of the form $\lambda_{n m}$ may be written $\mu_{n}$,
where $\mu_{n}$ denotes the cosine of the angle between the common
axis of $P_{m}$ and one of the axes of $Y_{n}$. The cosines of the form
$\lambda_{m m}$ will all become equal to unity, so that for $\Sigma \lambda_{m m}^{*}$ we must
put the number of combinations of $s$ symbols, each of which is
distinguished by two suffixes out of $n$, no suffix being repeated.
Hence
$$\Sigma \lambda_{m m}^{*}=\frac{n!}{2^{n} s!(n-2 s)!} * .$$
(47)
* \{We can see this if we consider how many permutations of the suffixes of one
term in the expression $\Sigma \lambda_{m m}^{\prime}$ we can form. The suffixes consist of 8 groups of two
numbers each, by altering the order of the groups we can form $s!$ arrangements, and
by interchanging the order of the numbers inside the groups we can form from any
one of these arrangements $2^{n}$ other arrangements, so that from each of the groups of
suffixes we can get $2^{\circ} \mathrm{s}!$ arrangements; thus, if $N$ be the number of terms in the series
$\Sigma \lambda_{m m}^{\prime}, N 2^{s} s!$ arrangements of the $n$ numbers taken $2 s$ at a time may be made, but the
whole number of arrangements thus made is evidently the number of permutations of
$n$ things taken 28 at a time, or $\frac{n!}{(n-2 s)!}$; thus $N 2^{8} s^{\prime}=\frac{n!}{(n-2 s)!}$, or $\left.N=\frac{n!}{2^{8} s!(n-2 s)!}\right\}$.
